nodes.content:
import pandas as pd

# OpenStreetMap's buildings in the loader's buildings box, a row for each
# building and each part of one, as Autark hands them on. Rasterize Buildings
# reads a "height" column in metres with a value in every row: the height
# mapped for the row, else its number of levels times the floor height, else
# the default height.
buildings = [!! input_0:table_osm_buildings !!]
height = pd.to_numeric(buildings["height"], errors="coerce")
levels = pd.to_numeric(buildings["building:levels"], errors="coerce")
height = height.fillna(levels * float([!! floor_height !!])).fillna(float([!! default_height !!]))
# What the nodes below read: building_id, which Autark gives every row of a
# cluster of buildings that overlap, the name, the height and the footprint.
buildings = buildings[["building_id", "name", "geometry"]].assign(height=height)
# Mark the frame as buildings, so an Autark map extrudes each footprint to its height.
buildings.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return buildings
nodes.goal: Give every building part of the loader's buildings layer a height in metres for Rasterize Buildings: the height mapped for it, else its number of levels times the floor height, else the default height; keep building_id, name, height and the footprint, marked as buildings.
nodes.title: Building heights

nodes.content:
# OpenStreetMap's parks, playgrounds and green spaces in the loader's parks
# box, as Autark cuts them at it. The named parks large enough to measure, in
# the open: a "park" mostly under the building footprints (input_1), such as
# a public atrium, is left out. Areas in metres, in the parks' UTM zone, so
# this works for any city.
parks = [!! input_0:table_osm_parks !!]
parks = parks[parks["name"].notna() & parks.geometry.type.isin(["Polygon", "MultiPolygon"])]
# A park mapped in pieces under one name is one park, its name its key in the
# comparisons.
parks = parks[["name", "geometry"]].dissolve(by="name", as_index=False)
utm = parks.estimate_utm_crs()
parks = parks.to_crs(utm)
area = parks.area
roofed = parks.intersection(input_1.to_crs(utm).union_all()).area / area
parks = parks[(area >= float([!! min_area !!])) & (roofed < 0.5)].assign(area_m2=area)
# One park mapped twice (two outlines that almost coincide, under two names)
# counts once: the larger outline is kept.
kept = []
for i in parks.sort_values("area_m2", ascending=False).index:
    if not any(parks.geometry[i].intersection(parks.geometry[k]).area >= 0.8 * parks.area_m2[i]
               and parks.area_m2[k] <= 1.25 * parks.area_m2[i] for k in kept):
        kept.append(i)
parks = parks.loc[sorted(kept)].rename(columns={"name": "park"})[["park", "area_m2", "geometry"]]
return parks.to_crs(4326).sort_values("park").reset_index(drop=True)
nodes.goal: Keep the named parks of the loader's parks layer (input_0) of at least the minimum area that are not mostly under the building footprints (input_1), a park mapped in pieces under one name as one park and a park mapped twice once; one row per park with its name as park, area_m2 and outline, in EPSG:4326.
nodes.title: Open-air parks

nodes.content:
import pandas as pd

# The building parts the what-ifs change, by one rule for every park, so the
# parks compare fairly: at least the Tall building height tall, and within the
# Distance from a park of any park. input_0 is the buildings, a row per part;
# input_1 the parks. Distances in metres, in the parks' UTM zone.
buildings, parks = input_0, input_1
tall = float([!! @tall_height !!])
utm = parks.estimate_utm_crs()
footprints = buildings.to_crs(utm).geometry
distance = pd.DataFrame({park: footprints.distance(outline)
                         for park, outline in zip(parks["park"], parks.to_crs(utm).geometry)})
marked = buildings.assign(nearest_park=distance.idxmin(axis=1), park_distance_m=distance.min(axis=1))
marked["around_park"] = (marked["height"] >= tall) & (marked["park_distance_m"] <= float([!! @park_distance !!]))
# What Height cap cuts a marked part down to: the Tall building height.
marked["height_cap_m"] = tall
# assign drops the frame's metadata: mark it as buildings again.
marked.metadata = {"layerType": "buildings"}
return marked
nodes.goal: Mark the building parts (input_0) the what-ifs change, by one rule for every park (input_1): around_park when at least the Tall building height tall and within the Distance from a park of any park, in metres in the parks' UTM zone; with each part's nearest_park and park_distance_m, and the Tall building height as height_cap_m, what Height cap cuts a marked part down to.

"""Rasterize Buildings: SCOUT's building rasterizer, "OSM vector to raster".

Input: a buildings layer, a GeoDataFrame of polygons with a CRS and a column
of heights in metres.
Output: one raster in EPSG:3395, each cell a height in metres: the 256 by 256
map tiles SCOUT draws, 8-bit gray where 255 is the maximum height, side by
side. A tile SCOUT writes no file for, because no building is near it, is no
data. An Autark map draws it as input_0, band band_1, and SCOUT's Deep Umbra
shadow model (Accumulated Shadow) reads it.
The Widgets tab sets the height column, the zoom level and the maximum height.
Ported from SCOUT, https://github.com/urban-toolkit/scout.
"""
from scout_rasters.node_outputs import rasterize_buildings

return rasterize_buildings(
    input_0,
    attribute=[!! attribute !!],
    zoom=int([!! zoom !!]),
    max_height=float([!! max_height !!]),
    output_file=curio_output_file,
)
nodes.goal: Rasterize the existing buildings into one zoom-16 height raster.
Predict the existing buildings' accumulated shadow with Deep Umbra.

nodes.content:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from rasterio.features import geometry_mask

# input_0: the accumulated shadow in minutes, a raster; input_1: the parks.
shadow, parks = input_0, input_1
# The minutes of daylight the shadow's season stands for, which Accumulated
# Shadow writes on its raster: SCOUT's 720 in summer, 540 in spring, 360 in
# winter.
daylight = float(shadow.tags()["minutes"])
minutes = shadow.read(1, masked=True).filled(np.nan).astype("float64")
rows = []
for park in parks.to_crs(shadow.crs).itertuples():
    inside = geometry_mask([park.geometry], out_shape=minutes.shape, transform=shadow.transform, invert=True)
    values = minutes[inside]
    values = values[~np.isnan(values)]
    if values.size == 0:
        continue
    share = values / daylight
    rows.append({
        "park": park.park,
        "cells": int(values.size),
        "mean_min": float(values.mean()),
        "median_min": float(np.median(values)),
        "p90_min": float(np.percentile(values, 90)),
        "pct_daylight": float(values.mean() / daylight),
        # Shares of the park's cells: in sun (shaded under a quarter of the
        # daylight), in partial shade, and in deep shade (over three quarters).
        "share_sun": float((share < 0.25).mean()),
        "share_partial": float(((share >= 0.25) & (share < 0.75)).mean()),
        "share_deep": float((share >= 0.75).mean()),
    })
return parks.merge(pd.DataFrame(rows), on="park")
nodes.goal: For each park (input_1), the accumulated shadow raster's cells inside it (input_0, minutes, EPSG:3395): mean, median and 90th percentile minutes, the mean as a share of the daylight of the raster's season (its minutes tag: 720 in summer, 540 in spring, 360 in winter), and the shares of its cells in sun (under 25% of daylight), partial shade and deep shade (over 75%). One row per park, with its outline and area.

nodes.content:
# Towers removed's shade per park, on input_1, minus Existing's, on input_0,
# matched by the park's name: in each number column, Towers removed's value
# minus Existing's, and change says whether any of them differs. A park
# only Existing has is removed, and one only Towers removed has is added,
# their numbers empty. The outline and the other values are Towers removed's,
# or Existing's for a removed park.
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

before, after = input_0.set_index("park"), input_1.set_index("park")
gone = before.index.difference(after.index, sort=False)
keys = [*before.index, *after.index.difference(before.index, sort=False)]
out = (pd.concat([after, before.loc[gone]]) if len(gone) else after).reindex(keys)
numbers = [
    column for column in before.columns
    if column != before.geometry.name and column in after.columns
    and pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(before[column]) and not pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(before[column])
]
was = before[numbers].reindex(keys).astype("float64")
now = after[numbers].reindex(keys).astype("float64")
out[numbers] = now - was
changed = ((was.isna() != now.isna()) | (was.notna() & now.notna() & (now != was))).any(axis=1)
out.insert(0, "change", np.select(
    [out.index.isin(gone), ~out.index.isin(before.index), changed.to_numpy()],
    ["removed", "added", "changed"], "unchanged",
))
return out.reset_index()
